display.title: True Ahavas Yisroel, Part 1
display.summary_short: Hakhel, Naaseh v'Nishma and Avraham's first command lead into a story: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev honors the funeral of a 'stingy' rich man and reveals his secret kindness.
display.summary_long: In a Hakhel year, the storyteller explains the mitzvah of Hakhel: after each seven-year Shemittah cycle, every Jew, from the oldest to the newborn, gathers in the Beis HaMikdash on Sukkos to hear the king read from the Torah, reliving Matan Torah at Har Sinai. He then speaks about kabbalas ol, doing what Hashem says even without understanding, as in Naaseh v'Nishma. Avraham Avinu's story in the Torah begins only at seventy-five, when he obeyed the command of Lech Lecha without a single question. Ahavas Yisroel works the same way: we love every Jew because Hashem said so, not only those we find special. The story: when David, a rich man of Berditchev known as a miser, passes away, the burial society wants to overcharge his family, but Rabbi Levi Yitzchak forbids it and attends the funeral, and the whole town follows. He then tells how David secretly gave 5,000 rubles of his own to save a wine dealer who lost his money, and later refused to take it back from the man who had really found it. Rabbi Levi Yitzchak promises two more stories, to be told next week.
display.lesson: Never judge another Jew by how he looks; love every Jew because Hashem commanded it, with kabbalas ol.
